papers.title: Diffusion-Based Imaginative Coordination for Bimanual Manipulation
papers.title_zh: 基于扩散的想象协调用于双臂操作
papers.tldr_zh: 提出扩散框架联合优化视频与动作预测，提升双臂操作成功率。
papers.cover_zh: 机器人双臂操作太难？这个扩散框架让成功率飙升32.5%！
papers.abstract_zh: 双臂操作在机器人领域至关重要，能够实现工业自动化和家庭服务中的复杂任务。然而，由于高维动作空间和复杂的协调要求，它带来了重大挑战。虽然视频预测最近被研究用于表示学习和控制，利用其捕捉丰富动态和行为信息的能力，但其增强双臂协调的潜力仍未得到充分探索。为了弥补这一差距，我们提出了一个统一的基于扩散的框架，用于视频和动作预测的联合优化。具体来说，我们提出了一种多帧潜在预测策略，在压缩的潜在空间中编码未来状态，保留任务相关特征。此外，我们引入了一种单向注意力机制，其中视频预测以动作为条件，而动作预测独立于视频预测。这种设计允许我们在推理时省略视频预测，显著提高效率。在两个模拟基准和一个真实世界环境中的实验表明，与强基线ACT相比，我们的方法在成功率上取得了显著提升，在ALOHA上提高了24.9%，在RoboTwin上提高了11.1%，在真实世界实验中提高了32.5%。我们的模型和代码在Diffusion_based_imaginative_Coordination公开。

papers.title: Let's Think in Two Steps: Mitigating Agreement Bias in MLLMs with Self-Grounded Verification
papers.title_zh: Let's Think in Two Steps: Mitigating Agreement Bias in MLLMs with Self-Grounded Verification
papers.tldr_zh: Verifiers--functions assigning rewards to agent behavior--ha
papers.cover_zh: Verifiers--functions assigning rewards to agent behavior--ha
papers.abstract_zh: Verifiers--functions assigning rewards to agent behavior--have been key to AI progress in math, code, and games. However, extending gains to domains without clear-cut success criteria (e.g., computer use) remains a challenge: while humans can recognize desired outcomes, translating this intuition into scalable rules is nontrivial. Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) offer a promising solution, given their world knowledge, human-preference alignment, and reasoning skills. We evaluate MLLM verifiers across web navigation, computer use, and robotics, spanning 13 models, 28 judge designs, diverse agent trajectories, and distinct downstream applications. We identify a critical limitation: a strong tendency for MLLMs to over-validate agent behavior, a phenomenon we term agreement bias. This bias is pervasive across models, is resilient to test-time scaling, and harms pipelines relying on MLLM judgments (e.g., self-improvement). We discuss principles for design and evaluation of verifiers, and introduce SGV, a method that improves verification by harnessing MLLMs'own capabilities via modulation of (un)conditional generation. First, an MLLM generates broad priors about desired behavior, independent of the data under evaluation. Then, conditioned on generated priors, it reasons over and judges a candidate trajectory. Our methods yield more human-aligned verifiers, with gains of up to 25pp in failure detection, 14pp in accuracy, and benefits extending to downstream applications. In self-improvement and online supervision, our verifiers boost task completion of a GUI specialist in OSWorld, a diffusion policy in robomimic, and a ReAct agent in VisualWebArena--surpassing the previous SOTA by 20pp. Finally, we release an updated version of VisualWebArena, featuring improved evaluators, high-fidelity environment parallelism with>10x speedups, and VWA-Lite, a 1/3-scale subset with comparable evaluation fidelity.
